bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Parent balance sheet as of 30th June 2026: cash and bank balance of ₹ 9,863 Crore against gross debt of ₹ 7,094 Crore; net worth (excluding NCI and capital reserve) of ₹ 17,375 Crore.
- Successfully completed a QIP of ₹ 7,503 crore "backed by marquee global and domestic investors"; the stated intent is "Leveraging Balance Sheet for inorganic growth opportunities in port and port-related infrastructure".
- Leverage at the parent: net debt/equity 0.27x in FY26 (from 1.17x in FY21) and net debt/Operating EBITDA 1.19x in FY26 (from 4.42x in FY21).
- Investment-grade ratings across Fitch BBB-/Stable, S&P Global BBB-/Stable and Moody's Baa3/Stable (newly secured), with domestic rating CARE AA+/Stable; in January 2022 issued USD 400 million 4.95% sustainability-linked senior secured notes due 2029.
- Parent consolidated guidance frames the reinvestment case: revenue ₹ 5,361 Crore in FY26 to ₹ 6,850 Crore FY27E and ₹ 10,800 Crore FY28E, with operating EBITDA ₹ 2,604 Crore to ₹ 3,000 Crore and ₹ 5,000 Crore (CAGR FY26-28 of 42% revenue and 39% EBITDA as printed).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Strategically located, large-format facilities with multimodal capabilities integrating CFS, ICD, PFT rail terminals, container train operations and warehousing into end-to-end logistics solutions
- Category 1 CTO License issued by Indian Railways enabling unrestricted, pan-India container train operation on both EXIM and domestic circuits
- Primary port relationship with JNPA, which handles approximately 50 percent of all containerised cargo volume among India's major ports
- Technology infrastructure including EDI connectivity, OCR-based internal tracking and GPS-based external asset tracking
- Post-acquisition access to JSW Group cargo flows, enhanced balance sheet strength and strategic alignment with a pan-India port and logistics ecosystem following JSW Infrastructure's October 2024 acquisition
- Early-mover positioning in Morbi, India's ceramic manufacturing hub exporting to over 160 countries, via ICD Morbi's rail-linked infrastructure
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Competitive and market fragmentation — The Indian logistics market is highly fragmented with many unorganised players; Navkar relies on differentiation through integrated, technology-enabled, multimodal solutions (Category 1 CTO licence, large-format CFS/ICD footprint, PFT infrastructure) that smaller players cannot easily replicate at scale.
- EXIM trade volatility — The ICD and CFS business is inherently linked to Indian EXIM trade performance, which is influenced by global economic conditions; mitigated by growing domestic cargo (35-45 percent YoY growth at Morbi ICD in FY 2025-26) to reduce dependence on ocean freight cycles.
- Geopolitical and trade-policy disruption — Ongoing Middle East conflict, US tariff policies and the Russia-Ukraine situation continue to introduce volatility in global shipping routes, freight rates and EXIM trade volumes, with a potential cascading effect on Indian port and CFS throughput.
- Dependence on Indian Railways infrastructure — Growing reliance on Indian Railways through the CTO and PFT businesses means disruptions to rail services, rake availability or policy changes could impact operations; mitigated via an owned rake fleet supplemented by leased rakes and relationships with railway authorities.
- Direct Port Delivery (DPD) competition — The growing share of DPD containers, which bypass CFSs and move directly from port to factory, represents a structural challenge to CFS volumes, though many DPD containers still require CFS facilities for interim storage and customs processing.
- Competitor capacity expansion — Increased capacity by competing CFS, ICD and rail operators, and development of new terminals, creates pricing pressure and potential market-share competition.
- Mundra Port congestion / rail evacuation efficiency — Increasing congestion at Mundra Port has at times affected rail evacuation efficiency from the Saurashtra hinterland; as Morbi ICD volumes grow, seamless rail connectivity to Mundra remains critical.
- Technology and cybersecurity exposure — As a technology-enabled logistics provider operating EDI, OCR, GPS and digital tracking systems, Navkar is exposed to technology failure and cybersecurity risks, mitigated through IT infrastructure, access controls and system monitoring.

business.body:
- Navkar is presented as part of JSW Infrastructure's "Foray into Logistics through Navkar and GCT"; the logistics footprint named in the deck is Navkar – Morbi ICD & GCT (Gujarat), Navkar – Ajivali CFS I & II and Navkar – Somathane CFS & 2 GCT (Maharashtra), alongside Arakkonam GCT (Tamil Nadu), Kudathini ICD (Karnataka) and a slurry pipeline in Odisha.
- The parent, JSW Infrastructure, is described as "India's 2nd largest Private Ports Operator & Fast growing Logistics Platform" with 186 mtpa ports capacity growing to 400 mtpa by 2030 and a market cap of ~US$8 Bn.
- Group context: JSW Group is described as "Amongst India's leading Conglomerates with a turnover of US$25 Bn" (as of FY26), spanning Steel (33.4 MTPA), Energy, Cement, Paints, EV, Ventures and Sports — the logistics strategy is explicitly to leverage these group business locations.
- The deck's own acquisition template for logistics growth is "Acquiring CFS and ICD businesses, akin to the acquisition of Navkar Corp", positioning Navkar as the reference asset for further inorganic expansion.
- The deck concludes the group is "Well placed to reap the benefits of the growing Indian economy, massive infra build, strong cargo growth potential and limited competition in the sector".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Filing basis] Navkar filed this under Regulation 30 as the "latest investor presentation released by the Ultimate Holding Company of Navkar Corporation Limited i.e. JSW Infrastructure Limited" — so nearly every figure is JSW Infrastructure group/parent, not Navkar standalone; only the slides explicitly naming Navkar Corporation are entity-specific.
- [Regulation] The deck details two Indian Railways licence regimes central to the logistics plan — GPWIS (launched 2018, general-purpose wagons, coal/cement/ore/petroleum) and LSFTO (launched 2020, specialised wagons for steel, chemicals, fly ash, edible oil, alumina) — described as a shift from a state-controlled model to a public-private partnership framework.
- [Anchor customer] JSW Steel is presented as the strong anchor customer, including a long-term take-or-pay agreement for the Odisha slurry pipeline and the 36 mtpa Dharamtar/Jaigarh expansion being predicated on a 5 mtpa steel-making capacity expansion of the anchor customer at Dolvi.
- [New award] Secured another PPP project at Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port with capacity of 0.9 million TEUs; also secured Environmental Clearance and rail connectivity approval to the DFC for Murbe Port, Maharashtra.
- [Sector backdrop] Indian port capacity is projected to rise from 2,810 mtpa in FY26 to 3,500 mtpa by FY30E and 10,000 mtpa by FY47E; infrastructure capital expenditure is shown rising to ₹ 12.2 trillion in FY27E.

business.body: Navkar Corporation provides comprehensive, customised, technology-enabled logistics solutions across Container Freight Station (CFS), Inland Container Depot (ICD), Private Freight Terminal (PFT), Container Train Operator (CTO), Warehousing and Equipment Pool business lines. It serves Indian and multinational enterprises across Manufacturing, Automotive, Chemicals and Fertilisers, Consumer Goods, Retail, Commodities, Tiles and Ceramics, Iron and Steel, Non-Ferrous Metals, Petrochemicals and Agri-commodities. In October 2024, JSW Infrastructure Limited acquired Navkar, making it the Company's ultimate holding company.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Container Freight Stations (CFS):** Import/export container handling, customs clearance services, bonded warehousing, container stacking yards, container parking and repair
- **Inland Container Depot (ICD):** ICD Morbi services for Mundra/Kandla-routed EXIM and domestic cargo, warehousing, Maintenance, Repair & Repositioning (MNR) for shipping lines
- **Private Freight Terminals (PFT):** Rail-linked cargo handling for steel, bulk, bagged, containerised cargo and automobile carriers
- **Container Train Operator (CTO):** Container rake operations on EXIM and domestic circuits under Category 1 CTO License
- **Railway Terminals (GCT):** Gati Shakti Cargo Terminal handling of export/domestic/BLC rakes

outlook.body:
- Continue to strengthen core businesses, improve operating efficiency, enhance customer service and pursue growth opportunities aligned with long-term strategy
- Deepen presence in Morbi, a key ceramic manufacturing and export hub, by placing rail-linked logistics infrastructure closer to fast-growing industrial clusters rather than relying solely on gateway-port infrastructure
- Advance initiatives to strengthen the Company's platform for future growth, including the proposed Gati Shakti Cargo Terminal at Somathane
- Leverage JSW Group backing for access to group cargo flows, enhanced balance sheet strength and strategic alignment with a pan-India port and logistics ecosystem following the October 2024 change of ownership
- Build a more resilient, customer-focused and growth-oriented logistics platform through disciplined execution under renewed management direction
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Navkar forayed into the Morbi (Gujarat) market during FY 2025-26, deepening its presence at ICD Morbi through focused business development and utilisation of its rail-linked infrastructure, with encouraging growth in EXIM and domestic cargo volumes cited as validating the move. The Company's Container Train business continued to expand its network and connectivity between industrial clusters and gateway ports. Under the PM Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminal (GCT) scheme, Navkar received the Letter of Acceptance (LOA) for a new GCT at Somathane, Maharashtra during the year, and is advancing this as a proposed project to further strengthen its platform for future growth; the Company already operates two other GCTs, at Somathane (Panvel, three railway tracks) and at ICD Morbi (five railway sidings).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's structural growth story — resilient domestic consumption, improving rural incomes, agricultural recovery and continued expansion of the middle class — expected to support logistics demand
- Government-led infrastructure development, including Dedicated Freight Corridors and PM Gati Shakti, expected to improve connectivity and supply-chain efficiency across the country
- 'China+1' supply-chain diversification and India's expanding manufacturing base under PLI schemes expected to directly support growth in EXIM trade flows through Indian ports and logistics infrastructure
- Encouraging growth in both EXIM and domestic cargo volumes at ICD Morbi cited as validating the Company's Morbi market-entry strategy and reflecting growing customer acceptance
- Container Freight Stations in Mumbai delivered healthy growth, while the Container Train business continued to expand its network and enhance connectivity between industrial clusters and gateway ports
- India's position as one of the world's fastest-growing major economies cited as driving increasing trade volumes, manufacturing activity and logistics demand
